sentences.text: The REST A P I tool is like handing the agent a menu and crossing out the dishes you do not want it to order.
You upload the description of the A P I and choose which operations the agent can use.
Anything you do not select, the agent simply cannot use.
In Tools, New tool, REST A P I, you upload an Open A P I specification in JSON, version two.
If it is version three, it is translated to version two automatically.
Then you improve the description, because the orchestrator uses it to decide when to call the tool, and you choose a solution.
Remember, a version three file converts by itself.
You select only the operations you want to expose: for example, create and get, but not delete.
You give each one a name and a description, and the descriptions of inputs and outputs must be complete.
This is how you give the agent only the power it needs.
There are three authentication options: none, A P I key, or O Auth two point zero.
With an A P I key, you define the label, the name, and the location, either header or query.
The user provides the key at run time.
With O Auth, you also enter the details of the identity provider.
If a question asks you to limit what the agent can do with an A P I, the answer is to select operations.
And here is the trap: uploading a specification without descriptions, because the orchestrator uses them to decide when to call the tool.
These are two easy ideas to remember.
